title: PLC Technician — Career Roadmap
summary: A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Technician installs, configures, tests and troubleshoots industrial controllers used to automate machines and production lines. The role involves PLC programming, input/output testing, sensors, motors, control panels and coordination with maintenance and engineering teams.

blocks.label: Recommended route
blocks.text: Class 10 followed by a relevant engineering diploma; Science with Mathematics is useful for alternative pathways.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Mathematics, Physics, basic electronics, electrical systems and Computer Applications.

blocks.label: Entrance exams
blocks.text: State polytechnic entrance tests, such as AP POLYCET for applicable Andhra Pradesh admissions; verify current notifications.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: PLC logic, relay circuits, sensors, motors, industrial control panels and automation.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Logical reasoning, troubleshooting, technical drawing, basic programming and electrical safety.

items.text: Diploma in Mechatronics Engineering → PLCs, automation, actuators, drives and integrated machine systems.
Diploma in Instrumentation & Control Engineering → Process control, sensors, transmitters and PLC-based systems.
Diploma in Electrical Engineering → Motor control, electrical panels, drives and industrial automation.
Diploma in Electronics Engineering → Digital electronics, controller interfaces and signal troubleshooting.
Diploma in Robotics / Automation → Automated manufacturing, robot-cell control and PLC integration.

blocks.text: For a PLC Technician role, prioritise hands-on programming labs, wiring practice, industrial networking and fault-finding exercises.
